title: A normalized derived scalar square from resolving representatives
statement: Let A,B,C,D be abelian categories with derived categories, F:A→B and G:C→D exact additive functors, S:A→C and T:B→D additive, and e:F⋙T≅S⋙G. Let LS and LT be functors between their derived categories with natural cochain comparisons εS and εT. Let good be a class admitting a quasi-isomorphism Q→P from a good Q to every P. If εS(Q) and εT(FQ) are invertible for every good Q, there is a unique natural isomorphism FD⋙LT≅LS⋙GD satisfying the square equation formed from e, the two ε maps and the exact localization factors, on every cochain complex. Resolving representatives use [lem-weil-pbc-reduction-pullback-derived-tower].

source.place: Tags 06XN, 06YY, 0D6D: localization on resolutions and composition

proof.text: On the full subcategory of good complexes the exact localization factors, εT, and e give one isomorphism to a common target; εS and the other exact localization factor give another. Fully faithful restriction to cochain representatives lifts their quotient to the derived functor category.

For an arbitrary complex choose a good quasi-isomorphism into it. Naturality of both square composites identifies the desired equation after precomposition with its localized image, which is invertible; cancel it. Uniqueness follows by fully faithful restriction and cancellation of the two good comparison isomorphisms.

lean.statement:
theorem resolvingScalarSquare
    (good : CochainComplex A ℤ → Prop)
    (res : ∀ P, ∃ (Q : CochainComplex A ℤ) (s : Q ⟶ P), good Q ∧ QuasiIso s)
    (hS : ∀ P, good P → IsIso (εS.app P))
    (hT : ∀ P, good P → IsIso (εT.app ((F.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj P))) :
    ∃! τ : F.mapDerivedCategory ⋙ LT ≅ LS ⋙ G.mapDerivedCategory,
      ∀ P,
        LT.map (F.mapDerivedCategoryFactors.hom.app P) ≫
          εT.app ((F.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj P) ≫
          DerivedCategory.Q.map ((NatIso.mapHomologicalComplex e (.up ℤ)).hom.app P) =
        τ.hom.app (DerivedCategory.Q.obj P) ≫
          G.mapDerivedCategory.map (εS.app P) ≫
          G.mapDerivedCategoryFactors.hom.app ((S.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj P)
